title: POC Toolchain & Benchmark Roadmap - Northpoint Logistics
summary: Discovery / POC scoping to agree success criteria, sizing and a short benchmark sprint to validate latency/cost for Northpoint's warehouse assistant use-case. Key asks: OpenAI-compatible API, function/tool calling to our orchestration, structured JSON outputs for downstream systems, and an initial 3-week benchmark + pilot timeline.
next_steps: Redwood to share POC checklist + example OpenAI-compatible endpoint mapping (by 2026-11-16)
Northpoint to export 3 sample workload traces & prompt set (by 2026-11-17)
Schedule 2-hour benchmark kick-off with infra and SRE (target 2026-11-19)
SE to prepare a sizing spreadsheet and suggested batch/quantization profiles (by 2026-11-18)
action_items: Alex Chen: Send POC checklist and pricing ranges - due 2026-11-16
Maya Patel: Build initial benchmark runner repo and example scripts - due 2026-11-18
Jared Lo: Provide tokenized workload traces and retention policy notes - due 2026-11-17

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-13
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Jared Lo (Northpoint - Head of MLOps), Priya Rao (SRE), Samira Nunez (PM)

AUTO-SUMMARY: agree success criteria (p95 latency < 350ms for 512 tokens, cost target <$0.003 per 1k tokens after batching/quantization), run 2-week benchmark sprint, validate function-calling to Northpoint toolchain, produce structured JSON schema for fulfillment events.

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros?
[00:06] Jared Lo: Jared here - I run MLOps at Northpoint. we basically need an assistant inside our ops console that summarizes inbound exceptions and suggests runbooks, and we need it to be predictable on cost.
[00:18] Samira Nunez: Samira - product. main success criteria from our side is accuracy for alert prioritization and that the outputs are reliably parsable into our fulfillment pipeline.
[00:30] Priya Rao: Priya - SRE. I care about network constraints and VPC peering, also SOC2 requirements.
[00:40] Maya Patel: great, Maya from Redwood. we'll focus today on SDK integration paths, the Open A I compatible endpoints, plus how tool calling maps to your orchestration.

[02:05] Jared Lo: quick context: current stack - we run a mixture of on-prem inference and cloud GPU for burst, but the in-house infra team is stretched. we're evaluating Redwood for a hosted/dedicated pilot first.
[02:24] Alex Chen: good, so pilot scope - are you expecting private deployment or hosted with VPC?
[02:30] Priya Rao: prefer VPC peering with dedicated capacity. data residency isn't strict but logs must go to our SIEM and keys handled by our KMS.

[04:12] Maya Patel: noted. On the compatibility front: Redwood offers OpenAI-compatible REST endpoints and an SDK. function/tool calling is supported; you can register tools that we call with structured payloads. slight caveat: when you use function-calling for high throughput you need to plan for larger payload sizes and KV cache behavior.
[04:36] Priya Rao: KV cash?
[04:38] Maya Patel: sorry, KV cache - the key-value cache for context. sometimes transcripts show it as "K V cash" so auto-transcripts like to mangle it.

[06:10] Samira Nunez: for structured output we need a fixed JSON schema: event_type, priority, suggested_runbook_id, confidence_score, and actions[].
[06:21] Maya Patel: that's straightforward. we can enforce schema validation server-side and return an error bucket for non-conforming outputs. in the POC we'll run a prompt set and measure schema compliance % and false-positive rate.

[08:45] Alex Chen: let's talk success metrics. I heard p95 latency and cost targets earlier?
[08:50] Jared Lo: yes - our SLA target is p95 < 350ms for 512 token responses in steady state. throughput target is ~120 qps for short alerts workload, and cost target is below $0.003 per 1k tokens once batching/quantization savings are applied.
[09:10] Maya Patel: ok practical note: 120 qps with p95 <350ms will likely need dedicated capacity; we can do a spike on hosted but dedicated pool or reserved capacity reduces variance.

[11:40] Priya Rao: security checklist - SOC2, SAML SSO, audit logs, KMS/HSM integration for key rotation. we also need paper trail for model/version changes.
[11:55] Alex Chen: Redwood provides audit logs, model version pinning and can integrate with customer KMS for private deployments. we'll include the security pack in the doc.

[14:20] Samira Nunez: benchmarks: what benchmarks do you recommend? latency at different batch sizes, p50/p95/p99, token throughput, and functional evals for schema compliance. also run cost-per-token calc.
[14:37] Maya Patel: exactly. our recommended sprint: week 1 - smoke tests and environment setup (VPC peering, keys); week 2 - run workload replay with 3 traces at dev/scale profiles, measure latency and cost; week 3 - tune batching, quantization (int8/int4), and run final verification.

[17:05] Jared Lo: on workload traces - we'll export ~5000 historical alert contexts and sample prompts. they include multimodal attachments references but for the POC keep to text.
[17:20] Maya Patel: perfect. small gotcha: quantization profiles can change semantics slightly. we'll run quality regression tests tied to your golden prompts so we can quantify tradeoffs.

[20:02] Alex Chen: question for Priya - network egress constraints? do we allow outbound to Redwood hosted endpoints from your VPC?
[20:10] Priya Rao: yes, but only to whitelisted IPs. we will provide a list. for dedicated/private we may prefer an on-prem option later.

[22:50] Samira Nunez: tool calling mapping: when the model calls a tool we want that to translate to a synchronous microservice call in our orchestration. can Redwood's function-calling map HTTP->internal RPC?
[23:04] Maya Patel: yes. we support registering tool definitions that call back to your webhook; we can do signed callbacks using your HMAC secret. for internal RPC we typically recommend a simple gateway shim that maps the webhook to internal RPC.

[26:40] Jared Lo: error handling is important - if a tool fails we want a fallback behavior that returns a best-effort summary and flags the job for human review.
[26:50] Alex Chen: Redwood supports fallback policies (auto-retry, model fallback, or degrade to shorter summary). we'll include an example policy in the POC doc.

[29:12] Maya Patel: For the SDK - you can use our official Python/Node SDKs. they have an OpenAI-compatible wrapper so minimal changes to your codebase. streaming is supported; also structured output helpers to validate JSON schemas client-side.
[29:30] Samira Nunez: great. how many code changes do you think for us?
[29:35] Alex Chen: probably a few lines to switch endpoints plus a little glue to handle tool callbacks and schema validation. Maya: can you estimate dev hours?
[29:45] Maya Patel: for a small team: 2-3 days to integrate SDK and webhook; 1 week for robust schema validation and error handling; that's assuming the infra side gives network access quickly.

[33:00] Priya Rao: what's the plan for model/version pinning and rollouts? we cannot have silent quality regressions.
[33:08] Maya Patel: Redwood supports pinning and canary rollouts. we'll run evals against your golden prompts pre/post rollout and surface regressions to the console with thresholds you set.

[36:10] Alex Chen: benchmarks - let's define the initial test matrix: 512-token typical, 128-token short, batch sizes 1/4/8, quantization off/int8/int4, measure p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec. agree?
[36:25] Jared Lo: yes. also include schema compliance % and a simple human eval for hallucination rate on 200 samples.

[39:00] Maya Patel: sure. for cost modeling we'll provide a calc: raw per-token exec cost + delta from batching + savings from KV prefix caching. note that caching is more effective for repeated contexts.

[41:12] Samira Nunez: timeline recap?
[41:18] Alex Chen: proposed: 11/16 - Redwood doc and pricing; 11/17 - Northpoint traces; 11/19 - kickoff benchmark; 11/19-12/03 - 2-week benchmark + tuning; week of 12/07 - review + pilot decision.
[41:35] Priya Rao: that aligns. can we include a security review session during kick-off?
[41:40] Maya Patel: yes, we can add a 30-45 minute security/compliance block in the kickoff.

[45:00] Jared Lo: small item - competitors: we've tested Anthropic for content safety and have an internal POC with another vendor. price/perf tradeoffs are the deciding factor.

[48:22] Maya Patel: we'll make sure to include comparative numbers where possible. note: exact numbers vary by model and sequence length, but we can run apples-to-apples on your traces.

[51:10] Samira Nunez: one more question on observability: can we get token-level cost breakdowns per-request and per-route in the console?
[51:20] Alex Chen: yes, Redwood Console surfaces token-level cost and latency; we'll enable a demo view for your team during the trial.

[54:00] Priya Rao: ok final wrap?
[54:05] Alex Chen: recap: Redwood sends POC doc + example endpoint mappings and pricing; Northpoint shares workload traces; schedule kickoff 11/19 with security block; Redwood SE builds benchmark repo; action items as in doc.
[54:25] Samira Nunez: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[54:30] Jared Lo: thanks.
[58:00] End of recording.
